title: Choosing ALB, NLB or GWLB
summary: Layer 7 routing, layer 4 performance and appliance insertion: picking the load balancer.
tldr: **ALB** (layer 7): HTTP/HTTPS/gRPC with path, host, header and query routing, Lambda targets, WAF and built-in OIDC/Cognito auth. One ALB with host rules can replace many per-service ALBs.

**NLB** (layer 4): TCP/UDP/TLS at millions of requests per second with very low latency, a **static or Elastic IP per AZ**, source IP preservation, and the front end for **PrivateLink** endpoint services.
**GWLB** (layer 3): inserts fleets of third-party firewalls or IDS appliances transparently using GENEVE. Need fixed IPs *and* ALB routing? Put the **ALB behind an NLB** as an ALB-type target.

keyFacts.text: **Least outstanding requests** sends each request to the ALB target with the fewest in flight. Use it when request times vary widely; round robin overloads some targets.
ALB **slow start mode** ramps new targets up gradually over a set duration, so instances that must warm caches or a JIT compiler aren't flooded.
On by default for ALB, off by default for NLB and GWLB. With uneven target counts per AZ, turn it on for NLB to spread load evenly.
An internet-facing NLB can take one Elastic IP per AZ subnet, giving partners a fixed allowlist. An ALB can't hold Elastic IPs, and its node addresses change as it scales.
GWLB passes traffic to appliances encapsulated in GENEVE on port 6081; **GWLB endpoints** in other VPCs route traffic through it.

traps: You can't attach Elastic IPs to an ALB; front it with an NLB (or Global Accelerator) if you need fixed addresses.
Sticky sessions make load *less* even; they don't fix slow requests piling up on one target.
Swapping an ALB for an NLB to save money loses host and path routing; consolidate ALBs with rules instead.
Deregistration delay applies to targets being removed, not new ones; warm-up needs slow start.
Slow start can't be combined with the least outstanding requests algorithm on the same target group, so pick the one that matches the symptom.
Classic Load Balancer is legacy and never the best answer for a new design.
